title: Flush the Buffer
goal: Extract the buffer contents while leaving the struct in a valid state.

source.attribution: adapted from Comprehensive Rust: Memory Management

hints: Moving self.buffer directly fails with E0507 because self is behind a reference.
Look for a standard library function that takes a mutable reference, steals its value, and leaves an empty String behind.
explanation: `std::mem::take(&mut self.buffer)` takes ownership of the buffer string and leaves an empty string in `self.buffer`. Moving `self.buffer` directly fails with `E0507` because you cannot move out of a reference. Passing `&self.buffer` to `std::mem::take` fails with `E0308` because `take` requires a mutable reference. Using `Clone::clone` compiles but fails the test because it leaves the original text in `log.buffer` instead of clearing it. `std::mem::drop` returns `()` which violates the `String` return type.
